sources.data_gov_in: api.data.gov.in (sample key by default; DATA_GOV_IN_TOKEN to enable live feeds)

kpis.name: Real Interest Rate (Saver's Yield)
kpis.insight_text: Positive means savers beat price rises; negative means money in the bank quietly loses value. Every 100bps of fall is a signal to lock FD rates before they drop further.
kpis.benchmark: RBI 10Y G-Sec vs World Bank CPI
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. Positive means savers beat price rises; negative means money in the bank quietly loses value. Every 100bps of fall is a signal to lock FD rates before they drop further.

kpis.name: Real Inflation Rate (Headline)
kpis.insight_text: The single most quoted cost-of-living number. Below 2% is stable; 2-4% is the RBI comfort zone; above 4% erodes real wages and usually triggers rate hikes.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. The single most quoted cost-of-living number. Below 2% is stable; 2-4% is the RBI comfort zone; above 4% erodes real wages and usually triggers rate hikes.

kpis.name: GDP Growth (Annual %)
kpis.formula: Real GDP growth, year over year
kpis.insight_text: Above 6% is strong expansion; 3-6% is steady; below 3% is a slowdown worth watching for job and income stress.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. Above 6% is strong expansion; 3-6% is steady; below 3% is a slowdown worth watching for job and income stress.

kpis.name: GDP per Capita (Nominal)
kpis.insight_text: Average economic output per person. It is the usual headline number global rankings use, but it hides inequality — always pair with the PPP gap.
kpis.verdict_text: Weak. Average economic output per person. It is the usual headline number global rankings use, but it hides inequality — always pair with the PPP gap.

kpis.name: GDP per Capita, PPP
kpis.formula: GDP per capita adjusted for purchasing power
kpis.insight_text: What the same output buys inside the country. The gap vs nominal tells you how much cheaper daily life is — which is why a ₹20 LPA salary in Jaipur buys more than in Mumbai.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. What the same output buys inside the country. The gap vs nominal tells you how much cheaper daily life is — which is why a ₹20 LPA salary in Jaipur buys more than in Mumbai.

kpis.name: PPP Gap (Nominal − PPP)
kpis.formula: Nominal GDP per capita − PPP GDP per capita
kpis.insight_text: A large negative gap means local prices are far cheaper than the exchange rate implies — money goes further inside the country. The bigger the gap, the more a remote or migrant salary is worth relative to its dollar figure.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. A large negative gap means local prices are far cheaper than the exchange rate implies — money goes further inside the country. The bigger the gap, the more a remote or migrant salary is worth relative to its dollar figure.

kpis.name: Current Account Balance (% of GDP)
kpis.formula: Trade balance + net transfers, as % of GDP
kpis.insight_text: A surplus means more money flows in than out (exports, remittances). A deficit above -3% is a warning that the country depends on foreign capital to fund its imports.
kpis.verdict_text: No data available yet.

kpis.name: FDI Inflows (% of GDP)
kpis.formula: Foreign direct investment as % of GDP
kpis.insight_text: Foreign money building factories, offices and infrastructure. Above 2% signals confidence; near zero means capital is staying home or leaving.
kpis.verdict_text: No data available yet.

kpis.name: Debt Service Burden (% of Revenue)
kpis.formula: Interest paid on public debt ÷ total revenue
kpis.insight_text: Every rupee of interest is a rupee that cannot fund schools, hospitals or roads. Rising debt service crowds out development spending — watch it alongside the fiscal deficit.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. Every rupee of interest is a rupee that cannot fund schools, hospitals or roads. Rising debt service crowds out development spending — watch it alongside the fiscal deficit.

kpis.name: Import Cover Ratio
kpis.insight_text: How many months the country can keep importing if all export earnings stopped. Below 3 months is a balance-of-payments crisis zone; 6+ months is comfortable.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. How many months the country can keep importing if all export earnings stopped. Below 3 months is a balance-of-payments crisis zone; 6+ months is comfortable.

kpis.name: Reserve Adequacy Ratio
kpis.insight_text: Can the country repay all debt due within a year? Above 1.0x means yes; below 1.0x means reserves alone cannot cover near-term obligations — a downgrade risk.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. Can the country repay all debt due within a year? Above 1.0x means yes; below 1.0x means reserves alone cannot cover near-term obligations — a downgrade risk.

kpis.name: Fiscal Deficit (% of GDP)
kpis.insight_text: How much the government must borrow to fund its spending. Above 6% is typically inflationary and crowds out private investment; below 3% is the FRBM target.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. How much the government must borrow to fund its spending. Above 6% is typically inflationary and crowds out private investment; below 3% is the FRBM target.

kpis.name: Power Demand Growth
kpis.insight_text: Electricity demand is a near-real-time proxy for industrial and commercial activity. Falling demand is an early warning that factories are idling.
kpis.verdict_text: Weak. Electricity demand is a near-real-time proxy for industrial and commercial activity. Falling demand is an early warning that factories are idling.

kpis.name: Index of Industrial Production Growth
kpis.formula: YoY growth in industrial output (factory, mine, utility)
kpis.insight_text: The cleanest read on whether factories are actually producing more. IIP leads GDP by a quarter — a falling IIP today is a slower GDP tomorrow.
kpis.verdict_text: Weak. The cleanest read on whether factories are actually producing more. IIP leads GDP by a quarter — a falling IIP today is a slower GDP tomorrow.

kpis.name: GST Collections Growth
kpis.insight_text: GST is levied on consumption, so its growth is a high-frequency read on consumer and business spending. Below 5% growth often means households are pulling back.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. GST is levied on consumption, so its growth is a high-frequency read on consumer and business spending. Below 5% growth often means households are pulling back.

kpis.name: Digital Consumption Velocity (UPI Ticket)
kpis.insight_text: The average amount Indians move per UPI payment. Rising ticket size means bigger-ticket transactions are going digital — a sign of formalisation and consumption upgrading. Track it with GST growth.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. The average amount Indians move per UPI payment. Rising ticket size means bigger-ticket transactions are going digital — a sign of formalisation and consumption upgrading. Track it with GST growth.

kpis.name: Foodgrain Production Growth
kpis.formula: YoY growth in total foodgrain output
kpis.insight_text: Food output growth. Two bad monsoon years in a row push food inflation up and squeeze rural incomes — the first domino in a rural distress cycle.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. Food output growth. Two bad monsoon years in a row push food inflation up and squeeze rural incomes — the first domino in a rural distress cycle.

kpis.name: Fertilizer Intensity (kg / hectare)
kpis.insight_text: How much plant nutrient each hectare of farmland receives. Too low means soil mining and falling yields; too high (above ~200 kg/ha) means overuse, water pollution and rising input costs.
kpis.verdict_text: On target. How much plant nutrient each hectare of farmland receives. Too low means soil mining and falling yields; too high (above ~200 kg/ha) means overuse, water pollution and rising input costs.

kpis.name: Irrigation Coverage
kpis.formula: Net irrigated area ÷ net sown area × 100
kpis.insight_text: Share of farmland with assured irrigation. Above 60% insulates farmers from monsoon failure; below 40% means a single dry year can wipe out a harvest.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. Share of farmland with assured irrigation. Above 60% insulates farmers from monsoon failure; below 40% means a single dry year can wipe out a harvest.

kpis.name: Crop Insurance Penetration
kpis.insight_text: Share of farmland covered by PMFBY or state schemes. Low coverage means a single failed monsoon translates directly into farmer distress and rural NPA spikes.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. Share of farmland covered by PMFBY or state schemes. Low coverage means a single failed monsoon translates directly into farmer distress and rural NPA spikes.

kpis.name: Bank Credit-to-Deposit Ratio
kpis.insight_text: How much of every rupee Indians deposit is lent back out. Above 80% is a fast-growing, credit-hungry economy; below 60% signals weak loan demand or cautious banks — often a slowdown signal.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. How much of every rupee Indians deposit is lent back out. Above 80% is a fast-growing, credit-hungry economy; below 60% signals weak loan demand or cautious banks — often a slowdown signal.

kpis.name: Priority Sector Lending Share
kpis.insight_text: Share of bank credit mandated to flow to agriculture, MSMEs and low-income housing. The RBI target is 40%; shortfalls mean credit is not reaching the sectors that employ the most people.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. Share of bank credit mandated to flow to agriculture, MSMEs and low-income housing. The RBI target is 40%; shortfalls mean credit is not reaching the sectors that employ the most people.

kpis.name: Gross NPA Ratio
kpis.insight_text: Share of bank loans that borrowers have stopped repaying. Below 2% is healthy; above 5% means banks are sitting on losses that eat into capital and choke new lending.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. Share of bank loans that borrowers have stopped repaying. Below 2% is healthy; above 5% means banks are sitting on losses that eat into capital and choke new lending.

kpis.name: MSME Credit Penetration
kpis.formula: Outstanding MSME credit ÷ estimated MSME GDP × 100
kpis.insight_text: How much bank credit reaches the MSME sector relative to its economic weight. India's MSMEs contribute ~30% of GDP but receive a far smaller share of formal credit — a large, persistent gap worth tracking.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. How much bank credit reaches the MSME sector relative to its economic weight. India's MSMEs contribute ~30% of GDP but receive a far smaller share of formal credit — a large, persistent gap worth tracking.

kpis.name: Hospital Bed Density (per 1,000 people)
kpis.insight_text: How many hospital beds exist for every 1,000 people. Below 2 is a capacity crisis — a pandemic or even a bad flu season overwhelms the system. WHO recommends ~5 per 1,000 for ageing populations.
kpis.verdict_text: Weak. How many hospital beds exist for every 1,000 people. Below 2 is a capacity crisis — a pandemic or even a bad flu season overwhelms the system. WHO recommends ~5 per 1,000 for ageing populations.

kpis.name: Full Immunization Coverage
kpis.formula: Fully immunized children ÷ children aged 12-35 months × 100
kpis.insight_text: Share of young children who received all basic vaccines. Below 85% means pockets of population remain vulnerable to outbreaks — measles, diphtheria, polio.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. Share of young children who received all basic vaccines. Below 85% means pockets of population remain vulnerable to outbreaks — measles, diphtheria, polio.

kpis.name: Out-of-Pocket Health Expenditure Share
kpis.formula: Household out-of-pocket spending ÷ total health spending × 100
kpis.insight_text: How much of all health spending comes directly from patients' pockets. Above 50% means a serious illness can bankrupt a family — a key driver of poverty and of demand for health insurance.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. How much of all health spending comes directly from patients' pockets. Above 50% means a serious illness can bankrupt a family — a key driver of poverty and of demand for health insurance.

kpis.name: Pupil-Teacher Ratio
kpis.insight_text: How many students each teacher is responsible for. Above 35-40, individual attention collapses and learning outcomes fall — a leading indicator of future workforce quality.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. How many students each teacher is responsible for. Above 35-40, individual attention collapses and learning outcomes fall — a leading indicator of future workforce quality.

kpis.name: Literacy Rate
kpis.insight_text: Share of people aged 7+ who can read and write with understanding. Above 85% is near-universal literacy; below 65% means large segments of the workforce cannot fully participate in a modern economy.
kpis.verdict_text: Moderate. Share of people aged 7+ who can read and write with understanding. Above 85% is near-universal literacy; below 65% means large segments of the workforce cannot fully participate in a modern economy.

kpis.name: Road Density (km per 100 sq km)
kpis.insight_text: How densely roads blanket a region. Higher density means lower logistics costs and better market access; very high density in cities often signals congestion rather than connectivity.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. How densely roads blanket a region. Higher density means lower logistics costs and better market access; very high density in cities often signals congestion rather than connectivity.

kpis.name: Vehicle Density (per 1,000 people)
kpis.insight_text: Vehicle ownership intensity. Rising density signals mobility and prosperity, but beyond ~300 per 1,000 cities face severe congestion and pollution — the point where public transport investment becomes urgent.
kpis.verdict_text: Off target. Vehicle ownership intensity. Rising density signals mobility and prosperity, but beyond ~300 per 1,000 cities face severe congestion and pollution — the point where public transport investment becomes urgent.

kpis.name: MGNREGA Person-Days Generated
kpis.formula: Total person-days of wage employment generated under MGNREGA
kpis.insight_text: Demand for rural wage work under MGNREGA. Spikes above 250 crore person-days typically signal rural distress — people are turning to guaranteed wage work because private rural employment has dried up.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. Demand for rural wage work under MGNREGA. Spikes above 250 crore person-days typically signal rural distress — people are turning to guaranteed wage work because private rural employment has dried up.

kpis.name: PDS / Food Security Coverage
kpis.formula: Active ration cards ÷ estimated eligible population × 100
kpis.insight_text: Share of eligible households actually holding an active ration card under NFSA. Below 85% means entitled families are missing subsidised food — a direct food-security risk.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. Share of eligible households actually holding an active ration card under NFSA. Below 85% means entitled families are missing subsidised food — a direct food-security risk.

kpis.name: Renewable Energy Share of Installed Capacity
kpis.formula: Renewable installed capacity ÷ total installed capacity × 100
kpis.insight_text: How much of India's power generation capacity comes from solar, wind, hydro and biomass. Above 40% signals a genuine energy transition; below 20% means fossil dependence is still deepening.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. How much of India's power generation capacity comes from solar, wind, hydro and biomass. Above 40% signals a genuine energy transition; below 20% means fossil dependence is still deepening.

kpis.name: Per-Capita CO₂ Emissions
kpis.insight_text: Carbon footprint per person. India's ~2 t/capita is well below the world average (~4.7) — a key equity argument in climate negotiations and a growing focus for ESG investors.
kpis.verdict_text: Strong. Carbon footprint per person. India's ~2 t/capita is well below the world average (~4.7) — a key equity argument in climate negotiations and a growing focus for ESG investors.

global_resilience.note: Ranked against India on real GDP growth where World Bank data is available. Current account and FDI columns fill in where data exists.
